Senses.Explanation: One half of the fixed pair of hall sayings from two heirs of the founding teacher's house: meeting someone, I come out; coming out, I do not do it for the person. Xuzhou Pudu raises the pair at his half-mountain seat and rules the two elders one eye and one arm between them, upholding the founding teacher's true line as not two, then sentences both great elders to thirty staff blows, Chijue Daochong raises the pair with the later master's ruling that the two old awls stole scraps of the founder's trade and marked off borders, then faults that ruling itself for knowing one side of two, holding the two elders put out one hand together and broke the founder's line for not a cent, and Xueyan Zuqin raises the pair and snaps it himself, one staff carried by two men and bent into two pieces by the Tianning master, then leans the staff to the left and lets each keep his half. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises the pair with the Xueyan master's verse on it, tells the assembly the verse has scattered the two elders' working to the marrow, and rules that whoever meets it can teach for people or not while whoever does not can neither, Fushi Tongxian gives each elder his season, one bowing to King Wen, one raising arms against Jie and Zhou, then reverses both halves at his Baoen seat, at times coming out and teaching for people, at times not coming out and doing nothing for anyone, and Jiqi Hongchu raises the pair with the Baiyun master's ruling that each elder has one place that lands, weighs the case as not without weight yet unable to escape the Fifth Ancestor grand-teacher's charge of clumsy words, and asks whether the founding teacher's family rule is anything one can bound, carve, or wander loose.
